 singapore Fewer low-income families received financial aid in 2025, but more money disbursed: Report
 Households under ComCare may have decreased, but the Government has increased the amount disbursed through the programme. PHOTO: AsiaOne file PUBLISHED ON November 16, 2026 10:00 AM UPDATED 39 minutes ago BY Khoo Yi-Hang The number of families under ComCare has decreased, but there has been a rise in total disbursements, the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) said on Monday (Nov 16).
 ComCare is a Government programme that offers both long term and short term assistance to low-income households in Singapore.
 The number of families has gone down from 20,825 in 2024 to 19,473 in 2025, while the total disbursements have risen from $94 million in 2024 to $95.8 million in 2025 for households which require short-to-medium term assistance, according to the ministry's Supporting Lower-Income Households Trends Report.
 Similarly, the number of households on long-term assistance has fallen from 3,240 to 2,997, while disbursements have gone up to $22.4 million from $21.4 million.
 "This may reflect a range of factors, including increased support through other Government measures such as the Assurance Packages," the report stated.
 The Assurance Package was launched in 2022, providing Singaporeans with cash, rebates, top-ups and CDC vouchers to help households defray their living expenses.
 The final part of the $3 billion enhancement to the Assurance Package was announced on Nov 10, with Singaporeans aged 21 and above in 2027 set to receive $100 to $250 in cash payments beginning in December.
 Low-income families achieve stability
 This comes as around 49 per cent of ComLink+ families achieved stability in 2025 across six domains: income security, children's development and education, housing, family functioning, health and financial resilience, according to the report.
 In 2024, only 44 per cent of families were able to achieve stability.
 ComLink+ is a separate Government programme that offers assistance to low-income families, providing participants with both financial support and guidance towards social mobility.
 The number of families that have or are receiving aid from ComLink+ has gone up to 11,006 in December 2025 from 10,219 a year ago.
 Additionally, the report also indicates that more families have been achieving positive outcomes in areas such as employment, preschool attendance and housing.
 Of the first cohort of ComLink+ families, 34 per cent of families had stable employment, were not on major forms of financial assistance, and had real income increases in 2025, up from 22 per cent in 2023.
 Thirty per cent of families in the first cohort had their preschool-aged children complete mandatory vaccinations, enrol in preschool and attend school regularly in 2025, which is an increase of 15 per cent from 2023.
 Lastly, 4 per cent of families achieved social mobility by moving out of their rental flat and into their own home — an increase from the zero per cent indicated in 2023.
 "Supporting lower-income families remains a shared responsibility," the report concluded, adding that individuals and organisations can play their part, whether by volunteering, contributing resources or partnering with the community to support families.
 "Through this collective effort, we can continue to strengthen resilience, expand possibilities for children, and help more families realise their goals."
